cues.text: Hello Dr Green - I'm here to talk to you about my work placement.
cues.speaker: HOLLY

cues.text: Oh yes, it's Holly, isn't it?
cues.speaker: TUTOR

cues.text: Yes.
cues.speaker: HOLLY

cues.text: So, which work placement have you chosen?
cues.speaker: TUTOR

cues.text: I decided to go for the Orion Stadium placement.
cues.speaker: HOLLY

cues.text: The event I'll be managing is one where I'm helping to set up a sports competition for primary school children.
cues.speaker: HOLLY

cues.text: Yup. That's always a popular placement - even though it can be tougher than you think working with children.
cues.speaker: TUTOR

cues.text: I know, but it's the fresh air that attracts me - organising something indoors doesn't have the same appeal, even though it might be fun.
cues.speaker: HOLLY

cues.text: OK, so obviously safety's going to be one of your key concerns for this event.
cues.speaker: TUTOR

cues.text: Yes, I've already thought about that.
cues.speaker: HOLLY

cues.text: I'll need to make sure none of the equipment's damaged.
cues.speaker: HOLLY

cues.text: Ah well, you'll be working with schools, so the equipment will be their responsibility.
cues.speaker: TUTOR

cues.text: However, the grounds and what goes on there will be yours.
cues.speaker: TUTOR

cues.text: Oh I see - that'll include keeping everyone within the boundary once they're in their kit and on the field?
cues.speaker: HOLLY

cues.text: Exactly - you'll need to inspect areas like changing rooms as well for anything someone can trip over, but your main priority will be not to lose anyone!
cues.speaker: TUTOR

cues.text: Right. I'll need staff to help with that.
cues.speaker: HOLLY

cues.text: And don't forget about the spectators.
cues.speaker: TUTOR

cues.text: Mmm. I was thinking that many of them will be parents, who could help run the event.
cues.speaker: HOLLY

cues.text: I wouldn't rely on that.
cues.speaker: TUTOR

cues.text: They'll be more interested in filming their children than volunteering.
cues.speaker: TUTOR

cues.text: I'll need to make sure they don't interfere with events doing that!
cues.speaker: HOLLY

cues.text: And that's not always easy, especially when a proud parent's trying to get a snap of their child and you want them to move elsewhere.
cues.speaker: TUTOR

cues.text: OK. What about the scheduling?
cues.speaker: HOLLY

cues.text: With sporting events there are all sorts of things that can alter the timetable - like rain, for instance - though so far, we've always been lucky with that.
cues.speaker: TUTOR

cues.text: Yeah, and I was thinking about what to do if someone got hurt as well.
cues.speaker: HOLLY

cues.text: I know that last year that caused a terrible delay.
cues.speaker: HOLLY

cues.text: You have to be prepared for such things.
cues.speaker: TUTOR

cues.text: Oh. What if a match ends in a draw - do you let the teams keep going until someone wins?
cues.speaker: HOLLY

cues.text: That'll be up to you - and again, you need to plan for it.
cues.speaker: TUTOR

cues.text: Right.
cues.speaker: HOLLY

cues.text: Now, the aim of your work placement is to give you the opportunity to develop the skills that an events manager needs.
cues.speaker: TUTOR

cues.text: So, let's talk about those a bit.
cues.speaker: TUTOR

cues.text: Well, I think my communication skills are pretty good.
cues.speaker: HOLLY

cues.text: I can talk on the phone to people and book venues and that kind of thing.
cues.speaker: HOLLY

cues.text: Good - just remember it isn't only about what you say.
cues.speaker: TUTOR

cues.text: If you meet someone face-to-face and want to persuade them to be a sponsor, for example ...
cues.speaker: TUTOR

cues.text: Oh, I'll dress up for that! Sure.
cues.speaker: HOLLY

cues.text: Good. Let's go on to think about your organisational skills.
cues.speaker: TUTOR

cues.text: You're working in a very people-based industry and that means things won't always go to plan.
cues.speaker: TUTOR

cues.text: I guess it's being prepared to make changes that matters.
cues.speaker: HOLLY

cues.text: That's right. You may have to make an on-the-spot change to a timetable because of a problem you hadn't anticipated ...
cues.speaker: TUTOR

cues.text: ... just do it! OK.
cues.speaker: HOLLY

cues.text: How's your time management these days?
cues.speaker: TUTOR

cues.text: I'm working on it - I'm certainly better when I have a deadline, which is why this work suits me.
cues.speaker: HOLLY

cues.text: Yes, but it's how you respond as that deadline approaches!
cues.speaker: TUTOR

cues.text: I know I've got to look calm even if I'm in a panic.
cues.speaker: HOLLY

cues.text: Just think to yourself - no one must know I'm under pressure.
cues.speaker: TUTOR

cues.text: Yeah-even though I'm multi-tasking like crazy!
cues.speaker: HOLLY

cues.text: Another skill that events managers need is creativity.
cues.speaker: TUTOR

cues.text: Often your client has what we call the 'big picture' idea, but it's up to the events manager to think of all the fine points that go to making it work.
cues.speaker: TUTOR

cues.text: Right, so I need to listen carefully to that idea and then fill in all the gaps.
cues.speaker: HOLLY

cues.text: That's right. And you'll have a team working under you, so another key skill is leadership.
cues.speaker: TUTOR

cues.text: Your team may have lots of ideas too, but you've got to make the ultimate choices.
cues.speaker: TUTOR

cues.text: Do we have refreshments inside or out, for example?
cues.speaker: TUTOR

cues.text: Isn't it better to be democratic?
cues.speaker: HOLLY

cues.text: It's a nice idea, but you have the ultimate responsibility.
cues.speaker: TUTOR

cues.text: So, believe in what you think best.
cues.speaker: TUTOR

cues.text: Be prepared to say 'yes', that's a good idea but it won't work here.
cues.speaker: TUTOR

cues.text: I see what you mean.
cues.speaker: HOLLY

cues.text: What about the networking side of things?
cues.speaker: HOLLY

cues.text: I know it's an area that a lot of students worry about because we don't have much experience to offer others.
cues.speaker: HOLLY

cues.text: But even without it - you can still be an interesting person with useful ideas.
cues.speaker: TUTOR

cues.text: And the more people you impress, the better.
cues.speaker: TUTOR

cues.text: I guess that will help me when I apply for a real job.
cues.speaker: HOLLY

cues.text: Exactly - think ahead - remember what your ambitions are and keep them in mind.
cues.speaker: TUTOR

cues.text: Definitely.
cues.speaker: HOLLY
